description:
Polish quality + latency eval set. Each item is a raw ASR transcript as Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 would emit it (already capitalised and punctuated per the NVIDIA model card) paired with the polished text the pass is supposed to produce. `bench_llm --eval` runs every item through a polish variant, scores word-level edit distance against `expected`, and reports completion percentiles over the same items, so the quality column and the latency column describe one population.

Category mix is chosen to match real dictation rather than worst case: most utterances need nothing or need one filler removed. The historical `bench_llm` SAMPLE_INPUT is retained as `legacy-bench-sample` so the 1225 ms p50 in bench/README.md §6 stays comparable.

categories.clean: Nothing to fix. Polish must return the input unchanged.
categories.short: Under 4 words. Prompt rule 6 says return unchanged.
categories.filler-light: One or two filler words. The common case.
categories.filler-heavy: Filler on nearly every clause. Worst case.
categories.command: Inline editing commands the speaker dictated.
categories.technical: Identifiers, versions, and code fragments that must survive verbatim.
categories.long: Multi-sentence transcript that exercises the output cap.
